title: Finite-order Picard approximation and projectivity
as_he_states: For a good henselian local base, compare the images of algebraic and completed line bundles at every finite order.
plausible_today: Use a noetherian henselian G-ring and a locally finitely presented moduli functor of the line-bundle data.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Artin1969 Theorems1.8/1.10 prove finite-order approximation for the specified excellent henselian settings; Stacks07QX states the henselian G-ring theorem. P32 then deduces descent of projectivity from approximation of an ample class on the closed fibre, using Stacks0D2S. This does not assert equality of algebraic and completed Picard groups.
why_open: The page gives a regular-completion criterion for good, with an uncertain arrow and an explicit algebraic henselization example; no later reason for abandonment is documented.
worth: Yes, as an exact archival comparison with approximation: first fix the moduli functor and its finite-presentation hypothesis.

title: Stronger comparison with isolated R¹ support
as_he_states: A stronger Picard assertion is proposed when R¹f_*O is supported at the closed point; the completed target is ambiguous.
plausible_today: Separate a proper-morphism formal Picard statement from a punctured-affine statement before imposing cohomological support hypotheses.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Artin approximation and Elkik1973 III.1 give different exact theorems; neither determines the uncertain X/Y target in this sentence.
why_open: The surviving arrow is uncertain; no source states why this particular formulation was dropped.
worth: Only after the scan resolves the target; otherwise one would research a reconstruction rather than his question.

title: Henselian punctured Picard versus completion
as_he_states: Does completion preserve Pic of a punctured henselian local spectrum, at least for an isolated singularity?
plausible_today: For a noetherian henselian pair(A,J), compare U=SpecA−V(J) with its inverse image in SpecÂ.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Elkik1973 III.1 Theorem3, Corollary1 and the following lemma/corollary on p.573 prove the map Pic(U)→Pic(U′) is bijective. The isolated-singularity restriction is unnecessary.
why_open: The page proposes resolution as a possible route; Elkik provides the later algebraization route. Her acknowledgement of Boutot is not a checked reading of his earlier work.
worth: Useful for commentary and provenance; no new theorem is needed for this exact question.

title: Separation and representability of the numerical quotient
as_he_states: The coset construction is expected to give a separated or unramified quotient under closedness/properness hypotheses.
plausible_today: For a represented quotient sheaf with faithfully flat quotient map, test separatedness by the closed kernel relation; scheme existence and unramifiedness require separate hypotheses.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: The diagonal criterion follows by descent; Kleiman2005 Lemma4.9 proves a specific quasi-projective smooth proper equivalence-relation quotient. It does not represent every quotient in the manuscript sentence.
why_open: The ambient Pic/Picτ notation is inconsistent on276; the page gives no complete general quotient theorem.
worth: Yes, as a short theorem-by-theorem reconstruction after fixing the ambient coset and the exact relation.

title: Represent the Néron quotient without representing Pic
as_he_states: It would suffice to know Picτ flat and closed, possibly without constructing all of Pic.
plausible_today: Distinguish quotient algebraic spaces from quotient schemes and specify which Picard sheaf is algebraic.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Kleiman2005 Remark4.18 states modern algebraic-space representability, while Lemma4.9 gives a scheme quotient under stronger hypotheses. No opened source matches the full scheme-valued hope without representing Pic.
why_open: The margin explicitly states a sufficiency hope; no historical explanation for its later fate is supplied.
worth: Moderate interest as a scope audit, beginning with the algebraic-space formulation rather than an unsupported scheme claim.

title: Equivariant correspondences and the Picard component
as_he_states: The quotient construction uses equivariant maps into A′; the correspondence functor is later marked yes by Raynaud.
plausible_today: For pointed proper families with universal O-pushforward and a represented rigidified Picard functor, isolate the correspondence factor; restrict to the appropriate connected/torsion component.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P22 verifies the rigidification formula and refutes the full-Pic interpretation. FGA236 and Kleiman §2 provide the functor framework; the exact relative correspondence theorem attributed to Raynaud was not located. SGA VI XII1.1 is a different pullback theorem.
why_open: A missing superscript and an unexpanded attribution obstruct identification, rather than constituting evidence of an unsolved theorem.
worth: High archival value: recover the component qualifier and compare the exact Raynaud functor before doing new geometry.

title: Four desired Hodge–Picard pathologies
as_he_states: The invariant-space formula is to produce four examples, only tersely listed.
plausible_today: Specify each invariant, base, fibre characteristic and comparison map; distinguish h¹(O), h⁰(Ω¹), Picard dimension and tangent dimension.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: FGA236 §2.9 gives nonreduced Picard schemes and a nonflat Mumford family. Oda1969 Corollaries5.11–5.12 gives the precise absolute Dieudonné/de Rham comparison. P11 shows the inversion control alone has equal Hodge dimensions.
why_open: The page announces examples without constructions; no source explains whether all four were subsequently realized in this form.
worth: High interest once the four conditions are made exact; one run can test the simplest invariant representation, without claiming all four realized.

title: Realize a p-divisibility jump
as_he_states: Construct finite flat subgroups whose quotient homomorphism becomes divisible by p only on the special fibre.
plausible_today: Require [p]F⊂G for descent and F_generic not⊂G_generic but F_special⊂G_special for the divisibility jump.

worth: High interest as an explicit construction task after the subgroup arrows are settled; the phenomenon itself is established.

as_he_states: Construct or lift the Picard part written Pic^{00|∞} over Artinian or reduced bases.

title: Flatness of Picτ
as_he_states: The page initially asks flatness, then records a negative answer attributed to Mumford.

title: Separatedness under weaker fibre hypotheses
as_he_states: Ask separation of Pic, Picτ or n-torsion under geometrically locally integral or separability-type fibres; mention a double elliptic fibre.

This supplies an exact positive case weaker than normality. The full merely proper locally-integral scope and the double-fibre model remain unidentified here.

title: Variation of Picard dimensions
as_he_states: Ask semicontinuity of dimension and of α,μ,λ, with inequalities whose primes indicate specialization.

SGA3 II X Remark8.7 states the α/unipotent inequalities for smooth finite-type groups and calls the merely flat extension probable. The general nonsmooth manuscript version is not certified settled or currently open by this bounded source set; the prime orientation is s special, s′ generic in FGA.

title: Auxiliary faithfully flat coherent module
as_he_states: Use a faithfully flat coherent module to extend the permanence statement.
plausible_today: Specify the module’s base, finite-presentation status and the descent data it is meant to detect.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: The opened formal-existence sources do not identify this terse margin as one complete theorem; it remains a formulation problem.
why_open: The auxiliary object is not defined sufficiently on the page.
worth: Low priority until the margin is read with its full surrounding diagram.

title: Removing quasi-projectivity
as_he_states: Hope that quasi-projectivity can be omitted, with doubt for the projective-scheme version.
plausible_today: Replace the ample-family/resolution argument by a theorem that actually applies to the intended arbitrary base.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: SGA2 and Raynaud provide powerful formal comparison, but no opened source matches the full weakened permanence/effectivity package. This is bounded non-identification, not a claim of current openness.
why_open: The author explicitly presents the omission as a hope.
worth: Worth a focused literature search after fixing whether the target is coherent sheaves, algebras or polarized schemes.

title: Necessity of flatness and proper support
as_he_states: Say the hypotheses are essential, request examples, and cancel a proposal to omit properness.
plausible_today: Test each hypothesis independently in a fully specified permanence or algebraization assertion.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P21 proves why proper support makes the nonflat/nonfree locus removable by shrinking. SGA2 XII retains the necessary finite/coherent inputs; no actual counterexamples to every missing hypothesis are supplied here.
why_open: The page itself requests examples rather than giving them.
worth: A good bounded examples task; begin with failure of closed-image control when support is not proper.

title: Fullness of the completed Serre quotient
as_he_states: Completion should induce a full functor from coherent sheaves modulo supports missing D.
plausible_today: The exact quotient functor is faithful/conservative; fullness needs depth or bounded-pole restrictions.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P29 proves exactness and the kernel description. P7 refutes unrestricted fullness using B_(x)⊂k((z))[[x]] and the series with pole orders n²; Raynaud1974 supplies a positive depth-controlled Hom theorem.
why_open: The manuscript strengthens a valid kernel observation into an unverified full-faithfulness claim.
worth: High value for clarifying the exact category; the unqualified version is already refuted.

title: Target-only depth in formal Hom comparison
as_he_states: The Hom comparison should depend on the target’s depth, not a matching source-depth bound.
plausible_today: A is noetherian local, quotient of a regular ring, complete for(t); P is its puncture and D=V(t)∩P. Require depthG≥2 at points closed in P outside D.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Raynaud1974 I.1.1/I.1.3 yields the exact isomorphism Hom_P(F,G)≅Hom_formal(F̂,Ĝ) after the closure-dimension reduction proved in P6; P5 proves the local Hom-depth inequality.
why_open: The source has heavy revisions, but this clean substatement is identified and settled.
worth: High commentary value; no novelty claim remains for this precise L58 formulation.

title: t-regular reduction and low-dimensional cycles
as_he_states: Kill t-power torsion, then impose revised depth and associated-cycle restrictions to get comparison.
plausible_today: Noetherian stabilization makes t regular on the quotient, but comparison still needs exact off-divisor depth and closure-dimension conditions.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P29 proves the torsion reduction. Raynaud I.1.1–1.4 provides precise comparison hypotheses; the manuscript’s erased/inserted dimensions remain a scan problem.
why_open: The final depth bound is blank or revised; t-regularity alone was not claimed to fill it.
worth: Useful after ink review; the first task is to measure every closure dimension in the correct punctured space.

title: Essential image and coherent hull
as_he_states: Describe the image of completion by conditions a,b,c′ and T₁, constructing a coherent direct-image hull.
plausible_today: Require an explicit extension to the completed affine scheme and a verified boundary coherence criterion; undefined labels cannot be supplied by analogy.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: SGA2 IX/XII and Raynaud I give exact existence/comparison theorems; P7 shows why arbitrary formal modules cannot be assumed to arise from the quotient. The full source corollary is not identifiable.
why_open: The referenced conditions are missing from the supplied faces.
worth: High archival but limited immediate mathematical value: recover definitions before proving an image theorem.

title: The reused formal-existence theorem
as_he_states: The printed theorem/corollary asserts algebraization in a projective relative ample-divisor setting; a depth inequality is partly missing.
plausible_today: Use precisely SGA2 XII3.1–3.2 with its fibrewise regularity, flatness and depth conditions.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: The two reused faces match those published statements. Their independent handwritten graded additions are not duplicates and are checked separately.
why_open: This is an earlier printed theorem reused as paper; the missing typewriter sign is a reading issue rather than a new unresolved theorem.
worth: Source identification is useful, but there is no new research problem once the exact printed theorem is attached.

title: Negative twists, duality, and the α direction
as_he_states: Analyze negative-twist vanishing by localization and duality; the text writes a surjectivity condition for α.
plausible_today: Exactness requires injectivity of α when the preceding restriction is surjective; retain the dual degree r−i and projective ambient hypotheses.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P4 proves the direction and P30 checks the duality route. SGA2 XII§1,§5 gives the published projective criteria.
why_open: The sign/direction error is internal to the displayed exact sequence, but the ink is undecided.
worth: High scan priority and low remaining proof cost; no broad equivalence should survive with the wrong direction.

title: Positive graded finiteness versus negative vanishing
as_he_states: Claim an equivalence between finite generation in positive twists and eventual negative-twist vanishing.
plausible_today: Treat them as separate properties and specify cohomological degree; the literal degree0 assertion is false.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P3 and the saved calculation give a skyscraper counterexample. SGA2 XII5.2–5.6 keeps the relevant ranges separate.
why_open: The page’s chain combines different questions; no authorial later correction is visible here.
worth: Useful for a corrected theorem table; the false equivalence itself needs no further search.

title: The inverse-limit interchange
as_he_states: Replace formal cohomology by the inverse limit of cohomology on thickenings.
plausible_today: Control the lim¹ obstruction, for example by Mittag–Leffler under the exact coherent-finiteness assumptions.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: SGA2 IX2.1 provides a uniform ML conclusion in its adjacent-degree finite setting; Laudal1965 gives derived-limit machinery. P30 records the exact obstruction sequence.
why_open: The page leaves the limiting step compressed or flagged; it is not formal for arbitrary systems.
worth: A useful proof-completion task: identify the specific system and prove ML, without adding a gratuitous properness assumption.

title: Scope of the starred depth condition
as_he_states: Use condition(*) near the missing boundary to infer algebraic/formal comparison; later warn sufficient conditions need not be necessary.
plausible_today: Specify whether(*) constrains interior points away from the divisor as well as the boundary; preserve the one-way sufficient implication.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P3 refutes the boundary-only reading when U=X and a skyscraper lies outside Y. Raynaud1974 gives exact sufficient depth criteria; neither chooses the ink interpretation.
why_open: The star’s referent is unclear; the source itself cautions against a converse.
worth: Highest scan priority because the two readings distinguish a theorem from a counterexample.

title: Twist-sign consistency
as_he_states: The final restriction map changes m to −m relative to its preceding argument.
plausible_today: Use a consistent twist on both sides of restriction and distinguish positive and negative asymptotics.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: SGA2 XII§§1,5 provides the separately ranged results; P3 gives a degree0 test showing why the sign matters.
why_open: Only the scan can determine whether the minus is present or cancelled.
worth: A scan task, not a new mathematical direction until the sign is fixed.

title: Coherence and the degree-zero hull
as_he_states: Relate positive graded cohomology, higher direct-image coherence/vanishing and depth.
plausible_today: For i>0 use R^i j_*≈H_Z^{i+1}; in degree0 retain F=j_*F|U or the separate H_Z⁰/H_Z¹ conditions.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: SGA2 XII5.2–5.6 gives the exact finiteness/vanishing statements. P30 checks the localization endpoint and why the hull equality is structural.
why_open: The page explicitly writes the hull condition; modernization risks suppressing it.
worth: Useful for a precise four-question chart; the first step is to retain degree0 as its own row.

title: Which cone has Picard group zero?
as_he_states: Several primed/tilde cones are boxed with Pic=0 questions; one is written SpecS[z] and another called projective.
plausible_today: Specify the affine cone, punctured cone, total line-bundle space and projective cone separately; for a reduced seminormal finite-type graded ring with R₀=k, affine Pic is zero.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: EGA II§8 supplies the exact cone models. Traverso1970 Theorem3.6 plus the grading contraction proves the stated seminormal affine case in P17; it does not identify the undefined boxes.
why_open: The missing object definitions are decisive; mathematical convenience cannot replace Spec by Proj.
worth: High archival value; the first step is an object-and-map diagram from the scans.

title: Factorial versus parafactorial
as_he_states: Assert factorial⇒parafactorial in the categorical setting.
plausible_today: Include depth≥2 and punctured Pic=0; a one-dimensional factorial local ring is a counterexample to the unqualified categorical assertion.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: SGA2 XI3.4–3.5 gives the exact criterion. P16 uses a DVR: A*→K* is not surjective although both Pic groups vanish.
why_open: The page omits a threshold or shifts between classes and categories.
worth: High explanatory value, settled by the exact criterion rather than a new conjecture.

title: Normalization defects and genus
as_he_states: Use g=1+Σg_i+Σn_s−ν; identify a multiplicative gluing contribution.
plausible_today: For a reduced connected proper curve over an algebraically closed field, n_s must be δ_s, the length of the normalization quotient. For nodal curves the extra genus and torus rank are b₁ of the dual graph.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: P14–P15 rederive the additive and multiplicative exact sequences; Ferrand2003 supplies pinching descent. A branch count is insufficient for a cusp, and xy=0 in three variables is a surface.
why_open: The notation n_s and ambient dimension are not fully specified by the drawing.
worth: Useful after merging the root’s earlier curve-normalization loci; no general tower theorem follows from the finite graph calculation.

title: The projective-cone Picard calculation
as_he_states: Correct Pic(X′)=Pic(X) to Pic(X)⊕Z and conclude Pic(Ĉ)=Z using EGA cone contraction.
plausible_today: Use the full section ring, Γ(X,O)=k, connected proper X, and a contraction f with f_*O=O; identify the hyperplane class and exceptional section.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: EGA II8.7.5 p.176 and8.8.6 p.181 were read and visually checked; the latter gives the direct-image identity under O_Y≅f_*O_X. P18 proves the conditional Picard calculation.
why_open: The source cancels the missing-Z formula itself; other cone labels remain uncertain.
worth: A good companion proof, contingent on identifying the model rather than silently changing the earlier Spec.

title: Picard invariance of a line-bundle total space
as_he_states: Pullback Pic(X)→Pic(E) is injective by the zero section; is it surjective?
plausible_today: For reduced seminormal finite-type X and E the total space of a line bundle, it is an isomorphism; seminormality is a sufficient added hypothesis.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Traverso1970 Theorem3.6 gives affine polynomial invariance, and P17 gives the descent argument using constant polynomial units on reduced rings. An affine cusp alone is not a counterexample to the source’s projective/full-section-ring setup.
why_open: The author writes surjectif(?), without the modern sufficient hypothesis.
worth: High potential for a carefully scoped example task: test the actual projective X and bundle, not a different affine example.

title: The cut-off R_p group-algebra theorem
as_he_states: For G satisfying the undefined(R_p), Q_ℓ[G] should be decomposed when ℓ≠p.
plausible_today: With Fontaine’s explicit R_p condition—normal p-subgroup and cyclic prime-to-p quotient—the statement is established.
state_of_art: Checked as of November 2026: Fontaine1971 §6 Corollary1 p.168, §7 Theorems5/5′ and §8.2 Corollary1 p.179 supply the decomposition chain. Brauer1951 p.250 gives hyperelementary Schur-index detection. The manuscript’s missing definition is not restored as an ink fact.
why_open: The reused printed page stops mid-proof and lacks its earlier definition.
worth: Low Picard priority; useful for identifying the paper stratum and avoiding a false Dieudonné connection.
